title: [Chapitre] VII. Analysis situs (troisième mouture) : notes manuscrites (23-26/06/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: this is Grothendieck's 1986 third version of 'Analysis situs'. Its basic structures are 'ateliers' and 'préateliers'. Each is a set M of 'figures' with two relations. The relation ≤ is the structural sub-figure relation (a face or sub-figure). The relation ≪ is a weaker relation of shadow-type containment: roughly omb(X) ⊂ omb(Y), where omb(X) ('ombre', shadow) is the underlying point set of X. The intended models are 'ensembliste' ones, where figures are realised in a set L of points. Two flavours are used: 'spécial' (affine) figures Fig(L) and polyhedral figures Figpol(L).

Page 58 showed a failure. Realising an atelier inside Fig(L) need not reflect ≪. Two strict polyhedral figures (e.g. simplices) can have X ≪_ens Y without X ≪_pol Y.

Page 59 responds by separating two notions:
(i) 'ensembliste' ateliers or préateliers, which satisfy the stronger condition (i), in the special or polyhedral variant.
(ii) 'quasi-ensembliste' ones, which satisfy only condition (ii).

He then states an intrinsic axiomatisation of quasi-ensembliste préateliers (M, ≤, ≪) with points x ∈ L. Here x ≪ X means x lies in the shadow of X, and x °≪ X means x lies in its interior. The axioms are said to be deduced from Prat 1'–6':
- Prat quasi 1: X ≤ Y ⇒ X ≪ Y. A sub-figure is shadow-contained.
- Prat quasi 2 ('densité'): every figure has non-empty interior, i.e. there is x with x °≪ X. This is non-degeneracy of figures.
- Prat quasi 3 ('divisibilité stricte minimale'): if x ≪ X, there is a sub-figure X' ≤ X with x °≪ X'. Every point of a figure lies in the relative interior of some face, as in the open-cell decomposition of a simplex or polytope.
- Prat quasi 4 ('raffinement induit'): take Y ≪ X and X' ≤ X, and put Y_{X'} = Ỹ ∩ X' (sub-figures of Y that are ≪ X'). Then omb(Y) ∩ omb(X') = ∪_{Z ∈ Y_{X'}} omb(Z). Pointwise: if x ≪ Y and x ≪ X', there is Y' ≤ Y with Y' ≪ X' and x ≪ Y'. Moreover, if Y ≤ X one can choose Y' ≤ X'; the two candidate index sets then coincide.

In words: the intersection of the shadows of two cells is covered by faces of one of them that lie in the other. This is the analogue of 'cells of a polyhedral or regular cell complex meet in unions of faces'.

Finally he notes that, in this pointwise setting, a separate incompatibility relation ∥ is no longer needed, since for points x ∥ y ⇔ x ≠ y.

Page 60 praises this structure as small (only ≤ and ≪) and common to the affine and polyhedral contexts. He envisages generalising it through 'admissible closed parts' with local finiteness conditions. He floats renaming topology as 'Stratologie' or 'Structologie'.

The problem served is a combinatorial, point-based foundation for a tame or polyhedral 'analysis situs', aimed at 'infinitely divisible' spaces.
errors: The phrase 'i.e.' in Prat quasi 4 asserts that the shadow-intersection identity is equivalent to its pointwise form. This only holds if omb of a family is defined as the union of shadows and points are detected by ≪. That is fine in the ensembliste setting but not spelled out.
The status of conditions (i) and (ii) (defined on earlier pages, not visible here) and the claim that Prat quasi 1–4 are 'deduced from Prat 1'–6'' are not justified on this page.
The notation Ỹ ∩ X' is overloaded: X' stands both for a figure and for the set of figures ≪ X'.
The closing remark x∥y ⇔ x≠y presupposes that points are figures with no common sub-figure. This is true in the set-theoretic models but is an extra assumption in the abstract setting.

ideas.what: Distinction between ensembliste and quasi-ensembliste ateliers, motivated by the failure of a realisation in Fig(L) to reflect ≪ for polyhedral figures
ideas.modern_name: faithful vs. non-faithful set-theoretic (point) realisations of a region/figure structure; spatiality of a point-free structure
ideas.usually_credited_to: spatiality questions for locales and frames: Ehresmann, Bénabou, Isbell (1950s–70s)

ideas.what: Axioms Prat quasi 1–4: shadow-containment relation ≪ coarser than sub-figure ≤, non-empty interiors, every point in the interior of a face, intersections of shadows covered by faces
ideas.modern_name: axioms for a regular cell or polyhedral complex as a face poset with point-set realisation (CW posets, face posets); stratified-space combinatorics
ideas.usually_credited_to: regular CW complexes / face posets: Björner (1984, CW posets); polyhedral complexes: classical PL topology

ideas.what: Using two relations, structural part-of (≤) and a 'significant' or interior containment (≪, °≪), to found topology on figures and regions rather than open sets
ideas.modern_name: mereotopology / contact algebras / de Vries algebras (well-inside relation); also loosely the way-below relation of continuous domains
ideas.usually_credited_to: Whitehead, de Laguna (1920s), Tarski (1929 geometry of solids), de Vries (1962), Clarke (1981), Randell–Cui–Cohn (1992)
ideas.where_published: The general tame-topology programme is in Esquisse d'un programme (1984), but not this formalism.

ideas.what: Observation that, for points, incompatibility reduces to inequality, so ∥ can be dropped

missed.claim: The atelier/préatelier formalism is a reinvention of region-based (point-free) topology and mereotopology. A structural part-of relation plus a containment/interior relation, with points recovered as minimal elements, is exactly the setting of contact algebras, de Vries algebras and the region connection calculus. Grothendieck's tame/polyhedral aims match work on polyhedral mereotopology (Pratt-Hartmann's mereotopology of polygonal regions, c. 2000s). The literature on Grothendieck's 'Analysis situs' notes does not, as far as I know, make this link. Page 60 even claims priority for working with 'lieux'.
missed.quote: Il n'y a plus lieu en effet d'introduire ∥, ou plutôt on la connaît : (x ∥ y) ⇔ (x ≠ y).
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It would place Grothendieck's tame-topology programme beside an existing mature theory: mereotopology, with representation theorems and polyhedral models. It also provides a ready toolkit for completing his axiomatics, e.g. representation theorems for the 'ensembliste' condition (i).

missed.claim: He gives a purely order-theoretic axiomatisation (Prat quasi 1–4) of point-based polyhedral or affine figure structures. This amounts to axioms for a face poset with point realisation, common to affine and PL settings. It was never developed into a representation theorem: which (M, ≤, ≪) arise from Figpol(L)?
missed.quote: Prat quasi 3 ∀X∈M, x∈L, x≪X, ∃X'∈M, x °≪ X' ≤ X ... Prat quasi 4 ... omb(Y)∩omb(X') = omb(Y') (= ∪_{Z∈Y_{X'}} omb(Z))
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: These are candidate axioms for the abstract 'tame' stratified spaces envisaged in the Esquisse. They could be compared with o-minimal cell decompositions and with Björner's characterisation of face posets of regular CW complexes.

deep.surprise_reason: The page holds a concrete unpublished axiomatisation from the 1986 analysis-situs programme. It is mathematically natural (face-poset and cell-decomposition axioms) and largely routine in content. Its interest is that it shows Grothendieck reinventing point-free/mereotopological ideas, apparently without awareness of that literature, a connection not recorded elsewhere.
transcription_corrections: The definition reads 'Un atelier est dit "ensembliste spécial"' (or 'spéciaux'); a little further on, 'en remplaçant Fig(L) par Figpol(L)'.
'Il n'y a plus lieu en effet d'introduire ∥, en qui la connaît' should probably read '... introduire ∥, ou plutôt on la connaît : (x∥y) ⇔ (x≠y)'.
In Prat quasi 4 the vertical '∨ / X'' under X means X' ≤ X. The hypothesis is: let Y ≪ X and X' ≤ X, and Y_{X'} = Ỹ ∩ X'.
The margin glosses are 'densité' (Prat quasi 2), 'divisibilité stricte minimale' (Prat quasi 3) and 'raffinement induit' (Prat quasi 4).
'(i.e. affinement spéciaux ou polyédraux)' is more plausibly '(i.e. affines spéciaux ou polyédraux)' or '(resp. ...)'; the reading is uncertain.
